Indifference Curves and MRS

This scene draws the indifference map of Cobb-Douglas utility.

An indifference curve joins bundles that feel equally good. Move the reference bundle and the whole map redraws. The marginal rate of substitution is the tangent slope there, as in the formula below. It says how much of one good replaces one unit of the other.

For example, giving up one 🍎 apple feels fine if you get two more 🍌 bananas. Then the MRS is two. The fewer apples you have, the more each apple is worth.

u(x1,x2)=x1ax21−au(x_1, x_2) = x_1^a x_2^{1-a}u(x1​,x2​)=x1a​x21−a​
MRS(x)=∂u/∂x1∂u/∂x2=a1−ax2x1MRS(x) = \frac{\partial u / \partial x_1}{\partial u / \partial x_2} = \frac{a}{1-a}\frac{x_2}{x_1}MRS(x)=∂u/∂x2​∂u/∂x1​​=1−aa​x1​x2​​
